papers.title: Translational Toxicology of N-Isopropylbutylone: Integrated In Vivo and In Silico Assessment of a New Synthetic Cathinone.
papers.abstract: The novel psychoactive substance (NPS) phenomenon represents a major global problem. Despite the methodical inclusion of new analogues in lists of controlled drugs, new compounds continue to circulate, frequently resulting in fatal intoxications. The emergence of N-isopropyl butylone (NiPB) in 2024, found as an adulterant in methamphetamine-based products, underscores the rapidly evolving landscape of NPSs. Despite its structural similarity to potent monoamine transporter inhibitors, specific pharmacological data and information on its effects in consumers are currently lacking. This study aim
papers.summary: This study characterizes N-isopropylbutylone (NiPB), a new synthetic cathinone that appeared in 2024 as an adulterant in methamphetamine products, using combined in vivo and in silico approaches. The authors assess its pharmacological activity and toxicological profile to inform risk assessment for this emerging novel psychoactive substance. The work highlights the rapid evolution of NPSs and the need for translational toxicology data on newly circulating compounds.

papers.title: Predicting Rates of Cognitive Decline in Older Adults with Brain- and Cardiac-Imputed Transcripts.
papers.abstract: Severe cognitive decline due to dementia is an important clinical indicator signaling neurodegeneration. Predicting cognitive decline rates can be useful in establishing prognosis and modifying treatment regimens. The rate of decline is highly variable across patients with dementia and may be determined by an interplay of many factors. This variability poses challenges to existing tools for predicting disease progression. Changes in heart and brain tissue have been associated with cognitive decline, yet tissue-specific molecular data are difficult to obtain. In this study, we sought to estimat
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint explores whether gene expression patterns imputed for brain and heart tissue can predict how quickly older adults experience cognitive decline. The authors use tissue-specific transcriptomic data estimated from more accessible sources to model variable rates of decline in dementia patients, aiming to improve prognosis and treatment planning.

papers.title: PCA-mapping and machine learning identify multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial, β-haematin and haemozoin formation inhibition activity.
papers.abstract: Inhibiting the formation of haemozoin remains a robust, non-genomic target for antiplasmodial drug discovery. While current efforts focus on multistage active compounds that are not pure haemozoin formation inhibitors, this class offers advantages including selectivity for Plasmodium and is associated with lowered resistance risks. With a view to developing cost-effective tools to streamline the discovery process, we developed a high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) workflow integrating both ligand- and structure-based techniques. Here, we employed a principal component analysis (PCA) enric
papers.summary: The authors developed a high-throughput virtual screening workflow that combines ligand- and structure-based methods, including PCA-based mapping and machine learning, to identify compounds that inhibit haemozoin formation in Plasmodium. This approach uncovered multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial, β-haematin inhibition, and haemozoin formation inhibition activity, supporting haemozoin inhibition as a viable non-genomic antimalarial drug target. The workflow aims to make early-stage antimalarial discovery more cost-effective.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Potential of the Edible Seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea: Bioactivity Coupled LC-MS/MS, Metabolomics Annotation, Validation, and Network Pharmacology.
papers.abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder with a global impact, highlighting an urgent need for effective dietary therapeutic agents for the development of brain-healthy functional foods and medicines. This study focuses on the edible red alga Pterocladiella capillacea from Zhanjiang, China, investigating its anti-neuronal injury activity, active principles, and underlying mechanisms. Methods: Based on antioxidant and neuroprotection evaluations and column fractioning, bioactivity-coupled liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (Bio-LC-MS/MS) was emplo
papers.summary: This study investigates the edible red seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea for neuroprotective compounds relevant to Alzheimer's disease. Using bioactivity-guided fractionation coupled with LC-MS/MS and metabolomics annotation, the authors identify active constituents and use network pharmacology to predict their mechanisms of action against neuronal injury. The work supports the potential of this seaweed as a source of brain-healthy functional food ingredients.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study shows that the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs determines how they disrupt membranes, revealing membrane interactions beyond carmofur's known mechanisms of acid ceramidase inhibition and SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibition. The findings suggest that tail length can tune noncanonical modes of drug action, which matters for repurposing and designing lipidated drugs.

papers.title: The Glyco-Code Molecular Template Instructively Guides Skeletal and Neural Development, Tissue Regeneration and Dynamic Repair Responses Following Trauma and Disease.
papers.abstract: Glycosaminoglycans encode instructional information that cells can decipher to regulate tissue development, repair responses, regeneration and recovery of tissue function following trauma or disease. This information has been termed the glyco-code and is a road map for tissue development and repair. This review shows that a clearer understanding of the glyco-code will support improved strategies in repair biology, particularly in skeletal and neural repair, regeneration, and therapeutic biomaterial design. Emerging therapeutic approaches for peripheral nerve repair increasingly combine multimo
papers.summary: This review argues that glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) carry instructional 'glyco-code' information that cells decode to direct skeletal and neural development, tissue regeneration, and repair after trauma or disease. The authors synthesize how understanding this code could inform repair biology and the design of therapeutic biomaterials, particularly for peripheral nerve repair.

papers.title: In Vitro Anticancer Activity and Integrated Multi-Target Computational Analysis of Ylang-Ylang Essential Oil Against Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Ylang-ylang essential oil (YEO), obtained from Cananga odorata, contains chemically diverse constituents with potential anticancer activity that warrants further investigation. This study investigated the anti-breast-cancer potential of YEO through an integrated experimental and computational approach. The essential oil was chemically characterized by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, and its in vitro cytotoxic activity was evaluated against ER-positive MCF-7 and triple-negative MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-436 breast-cancer cell lines using the MTT assay. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were
papers.summary: This study characterizes the chemical composition of ylang-ylang essential oil and tests its cytotoxic effects against ER-positive and triple-negative breast cancer cell lines, finding selective anticancer activity. The authors complement the in vitro MTT assays with computational multi-target analysis to predict molecular mechanisms and protein targets underlying the observed effects.

papers.title: A Drug-Referenced Machine-Learning Framework for Prioritizing Korean Herbal Formulations in Hypertension Using Linear SVM and Graph Convolutional Networks.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is regulated by interacting molecular systems, providing a rationale for network-based screening of multicomponent therapeutic candidates. Grounded in the conceptual framework of network pharmacology, we developed a hypertension-focused computational framework to prioritize insurance-covered Korean herbal formulations using protein-protein interaction networks derived from marketed antihypertensive and comparator drugs. Thirty reference-drug graphs (15 antihypertensive and 15 comparator drugs) were evaluated using four molecular classifiers under repeated group-aware nested cross-
papers.summary: The authors built a computational framework that uses protein-protein interaction networks from known antihypertensive drugs to rank Korean herbal formulations for hypertension. They compared four classifiers, including linear SVM and graph convolutional networks, on 30 reference-drug graphs (15 antihypertensives and 15 comparators) to identify formulations with drug-like network signatures. The work is a proof-of-concept for network-pharmacology-based prioritization of multicomponent herbal candidates.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Novel Therapeutic Opportunities in Precision Oncology.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping molecular oncology by making complex biological data tractable and by extending the reach of precision drug discovery. Its emerging value is particularly evident at the interface of immunoengineering and targeted therapy, where computational models can help prioritize tumor-selective antigens, predict neoantigen immunogenicity, optimize engineered receptors, support antibody and antibody-drug conjugate design, guide small-molecule discovery, refine genome-editing strategies, and anticipate treatment response. Across these applications, the central prom
papers.summary: This review argues that AI is becoming a practical catalyst across precision oncology, particularly where immunoengineering meets targeted therapy. It surveys computational approaches for prioritizing tumor-selective antigens, predicting neoantigen immunogenicity, optimizing engineered receptors, designing antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates, guiding small-molecule discovery, refining genome editing, and anticipating treatment response. The central premise is that AI makes complex biological data tractable enough to accelerate and de-risk therapeutic development.

papers.title: Quinazoline-tethered thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors: green synthesis, molecular docking, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-fused heterocycles have attracted considerable research interest in pharmaceutical, medicinal, organometallic, and materials chemistry. In this work, two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives were synthesized using choline hydroxide as an environmentally friendly catalyst. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT). Compound 11e showed the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 0.599 µg mL-1 (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was performed to examine
papers.summary: This paper reports a green synthesis route using choline hydroxide as a catalyst to produce two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives, which were then tested as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors. The most potent compound, 11e, inhibited HIV-1 RT with an IC50 of 0.599 µg/mL (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was used to explore how these compounds bind to the target enzyme.

papers.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Investigation of Fluorinated Benzoylthiourea Derivatives: Structural Characterization, Hirshfeld Surface Analysis, Antioxidant Activity, and MAO-B Inhibitory Potential for Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Three novel fluorinated benzoylthiourea derivatives, namely FBTU1-FBTU3, were successfully synthesized in 79-86% yields and fully characterized using spectroscopic techniques including FT-IR, 1H, 13C and 19F NMR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, elemental analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). All three compounds crystallize in the monoclinic system (P21/c for FBTU1 and FBTU3; P21/n for FBTU2) with Z = 4. The crystallographic analysis revealed well-defined molecular geometries stabilized by intramolecular and intermolecular interactions. Hirshfeld surface and energy framework analyses ind
papers.summary: Three new fluorinated benzoylthiourea compounds were synthesized and characterized by spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography, with crystal packing analyzed via Hirshfeld surfaces. The compounds were evaluated for antioxidant activity and MAO-B inhibition, a target relevant to Parkinson's disease, using combined experimental and computational docking approaches. The work is a structure-activity study of a small compound series rather than a broad methodological advance.

papers.title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists.
papers.abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.
papers.summary: This perspective reviews how large language model-driven AI agents are moving drug discovery beyond task-specific tools toward autonomous 'virtual scientists.' The authors propose a 6-level 'Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy' to gauge system maturity and argue for evaluation paradigms based on full-chain traceability, while outlining adoption barriers and positioning agents as scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning framework for peptide lead optimization in ultralarge design spaces.
papers.abstract: In modern peptide drug discovery, the incorporation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) has become a powerful strategy to improve potency and key developability properties, including stability, solubility, and oral bioavailability. This shift has expanded peptide chemical diversity and design spaces well beyond natural residues, creating fundamental challenges for predictive methods (e.g., quantitative structure-activity relationship modeling) used in lead optimization: limited transferability from natural residues to novel ncAAs, limited interpretability, and poor scalability to ultralarge pe
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable machine learning framework for optimizing peptide drug candidates that incorporate noncanonical amino acids, addressing the challenge of predicting properties in chemical spaces far larger than those spanned by natural residues. The approach aims to improve transferability, interpretability, and scalability of quantitative structure-activity relationship modeling for peptide lead optimization. It targets practical peptide drug discovery where noncanonical residues are used to enhance potency, stability, solubility, and oral bioavailability.

papers.title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Bo
papers.summary: This study prospectively tested deep-learning co-folding methods (including AlphaFold3) on 489 newly determined ligand-bound structures of the SARS-CoV-2 Mac1 domain, all solved after the models' training cutoffs to ensure true independence. The authors also ran three virtual screens, finding that while co-folding can predict ligand-bound complex structures reasonably well, ranking ligands by binding affinity remains a major weakness. The work provides a rigorous, large-scale benchmark for how well these tools generalize to unseen complexes.

papers.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1 and structure-based drug design by buckwheat derived compounds.
papers.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Sheikh et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. AKT1 is a serine-threonine protein-kinase involved in tumour cell proliferation, survival, metabolism, and therapeutic resistance via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. However, the comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of AKT1 and systematics identifications of natural AKT1 inhibitors remains limited. T
papers.summary: This study performs an integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1, a kinase central to the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, characterizing its expression and alterations across tumor types. The authors then use structure-based drug design to identify buckwheat-derived natural compounds as potential AKT1 inhibitors. The work combines cancer genomics with computational docking to propose plant-derived candidates for AKT1-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Transforming the Landscape of Drug Innovation in AI Era: AlphaFold 3 and Beyond.
papers.abstract: The traditional drug discovery and development (DDD) pipeline has long been characterized by inefficiency and high costs. The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), especially AI-based toolkits for protein structure and interaction prediction, exemplified by AlphaFold 3 (AF3), promises to reshape the landscape of drug innovation. AF3 advances structural biology by predicting protein structures and their interactions with a range of biomolecules, including nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially changing the conventional DDD paradigm, although prediction accuracy
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI-based protein structure and interaction prediction tools, particularly AlphaFold 3, are reshaping the drug discovery and development pipeline. AF3 extends beyond protein structure prediction to modeling interactions with nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially transforming the traditional costly and inefficient DDD paradigm, though prediction accuracy remains a limitation.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Brightfield Detection of Anti-Fibrotic Effects in a 3D Retinal Fibrosis Model.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spheroid and microtissue models are increasingly used in phenotypic drug discovery, yet their scalability for high-throughput screening often remains limited, constrained by the cost and complexity of conventional imaging-based readouts. Here, we present a morphology-based screening approach using low-resolution brightfield images of human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues (hRPE-MTs) to identify fibrotic and non-fibrotic phenotypes. The results of this study demonstrate that extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids enables quan
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study shows that low-resolution brightfield images of 3D human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues can be analyzed with machine learning to distinguish fibrotic from non-fibrotic phenotypes. By extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids, the authors enable a cheaper, more scalable readout for phenotypic drug screening than conventional imaging. The approach supports detection of anti-fibrotic effects in a 3D retinal fibrosis model.

papers.title: TechBio 3.0 closes the drug discovery loop with multimodal AI and generative chemistry.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed molecular prediction and design, yet these advances remain only partially integrated with experimental discovery. We define TechBio 3.0 as an emerging paradigm for closed-loop drug discovery that connects multimodal molecular representations, generative chemistry, and automated experimentation. We examine its early preclinical and clinical evidence, identify remaining technical and translational barriers, and argue that this convergence is beginning to define biotechnology's next era.
papers.summary: This perspective defines TechBio 3.0 as an emerging paradigm that closes the drug discovery loop by integrating multimodal molecular representations, generative chemistry, and automated experimentation. The authors review early preclinical and clinical evidence for this convergence, identify remaining technical and translational barriers, and argue it is beginning to define biotechnology's next era.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the structure of the antifungal protein NFAP2, which binds fungus-specific intracellular targets like glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase, to guide structure-based drug repurposing against Candida albicans. By screening existing compounds against these protein targets, the authors identify candidates that could be repurposed as antifungals, offering a faster route to new treatments given rising resistance and limited options.

papers.title: Using structure to evaluate the accuracy and transferability of machine learning potentials of biomolecules.
papers.abstract: Molecular simulation is a powerful tool to describe chemical and physical processes across length scales. Fundamental tradeoffs between the accuracy of quantum mechanics and speed of classical models makes simulating biosystems very difficult. Machine learning potentials (MLPs) offer a potential solution which combines the accuracy of electronic structure theory with the computational scaling of classical approaches. Applying MLPs to biosystems could unlock new developments in drug discovery, biological mechanisms and interactions. Despite this promise, rigorous benchmarks are needed to determ
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks machine learning potentials (MLPs) for biomolecules by using structural accuracy as a metric to assess both their precision and their transferability to new systems. The authors argue that rigorous evaluation is needed before MLPs can be reliably applied to biosystems such as drug discovery and biological mechanism studies. The work provides a framework for judging how well MLPs generalize beyond their training data.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream position, which leaves them without a closed molecular reference and without the standardized, readily model
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of AI in mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics across three generations: classical chemometrics/machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with LLMs currently playing only peripheral roles. It argues that despite being the omics layers closest to drug action, metabolomics and lipidomics have lagged in AI adoption due to their downstream position, lack of a closed molecular reference, and absence of standardized, model-ready data.

papers.title: Design and Synthesis of New Thiazole Derivatives for Alzheimer's Disease Therapy as a Potential Cholinesterase Inhibitor; Toxicity Prediction and Molecular Docking Studies and Biological Evaluation.
papers.abstract: In this study, thiazole derivatives 13-23 were synthesized as novel cholinesterase inhibitors. Their structures were elucidated using 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and elemental analysis techniques. The binding positions and efficiencies of the designed compounds on the enzyme were investigated through molecular docking studies, and the properties of ADMET were examined using computational methods. Cytotoxicity analyses of the synthesized compounds were performed to screen their inhibitory effects on acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) in vitro. It has been determined that these co
papers.summary: This study reports the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a series of thiazole derivatives (13-23) as novel cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease therapy. The compounds were characterized by NMR and elemental analysis, and their binding to acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase was assessed via molecular docking, ADMET predictions, and in vitro enzyme inhibition and cytotoxicity assays. The work identifies thiazole scaffolds with potential dual cholinesterase inhibitory activity, though the abstract is truncated and specific potency data are not provided.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used GNPS molecular networking of LC-HRMS/MS data to profile the metabolites of Scoparia dulcis aerial parts, then combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations with experimental validation to identify bioactive constituents and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The work links specific phytochemicals to inflammatory targets and pathways, providing a mechanistic basis for the traditional use of this edible herb.

papers.title: Sartans and Bisartans: Expanding Therapeutic Horizons Through Broad Receptor Interactions and Repurposing Potential.
papers.abstract: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), also known as sartans, are a family of highly selective angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonists commonly prescribed to individuals with hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Additionally, the discovery and facile synthesis of bisartans, a novel class of ARB antihypertensives, have shown therapeutic promise for cardiovascular diseases. Recent computational and network pharmacology studies have shown a broader receptor interactome, encompassing alpha-adrenergic receptors, and delta- and mu-opioid receptors, highlighting the polypharmaco
papers.summary: This review examines angiotensin receptor blockers (sartans) and the newer bisartans, highlighting that beyond their canonical AT1 receptor blockade, computational and network pharmacology studies suggest they interact with alpha-adrenergic and delta/mu-opioid receptors. This broader receptor interactome points to polypharmacology that may support drug repurposing for additional therapeutic indications.

papers.title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski r
papers.summary: This study evaluates PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, as a potential efflux pump inhibitor against MRSA using combined computational (docking, molecular dynamics, Lipinski rule analysis) and in vitro approaches. The work targets NorA and MepA efflux pumps, which reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute to resistance. The integrated methodology aims to identify whether PBSA-7 can restore antibiotic efficacy by blocking these pumps.

papers.title: Thymol-based derivatives as anticancer agents: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Seventeen thymol-based derivatives (TM1-7, TBr1-2, TCl1-4, and TF1-4) were designed and synthesized by esterification with halo- and non-halogenated cinnamoyl molecules employing a key-step coupling reaction. All derivatives were chemically characterized (1H NMR, 13C NMR, HR-MS, and HPLC analysis) and evaluated for their potential anticancer properties. The anti-proliferative effectiveness was assessed using an MTT assay against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, and JIMT1) and human dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) compared to Triton X-100. Among the thymol-based derivatives, TM7 an
papers.summary: The authors synthesized seventeen thymol-based ester derivatives using cinnamoyl coupling chemistry and screened them for anticancer activity against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, JIMT1) and normal human dermal fibroblasts. One derivative, TM7, emerged as the most promising antiproliferative agent, and molecular docking was used to rationalize its binding to a likely biological target. The work is a standard medicinal chemistry structure-activity study identifying a lead compound for further optimization.

papers.title: Discovery and biological characterization of 1-[4-(2-difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A novel thiazolyl-urea chemotype targeting yellow fever virus and host casein kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: The authors synthesized and characterized a novel thiazolyl-urea compound, DFMNTU, and showed it inhibits yellow fever virus (strain 17D) in Vero cells while targeting the host kinase CK2, suggesting a host-directed antiviral strategy. This is an early-stage medicinal chemistry and in vitro virology study identifying a new chemotype rather than a validated drug.

papers.title: Design-Evolution Synergy Enables New-to-Nature Enzyme Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution and machine-learning-assisted evolution have transformed biocatalysis by enabling rapid optimisation of catalytic performance within compatible protein scaffolds. In parallel, advances in deep-learning-driven de novo protein design have expanded accessible protein architectural space, enabling the generation of functional catalysts for increasingly challenging transformations. We herein report a synergistic design-evolution strategy to encode new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination reactions using engineered de novo haemproteins to synthesise chiral piperidin
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint combines deep-learning-driven de novo protein design with directed evolution to create engineered haemoproteins that catalyse new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination, enabling synthesis of chiral piperidines. The work demonstrates that design and evolution can be used synergistically rather than sequentially to access enzyme chemistry not found in nature.

papers.title: ProDTI: prior-guided positive-unlabeled learning for robust drug-target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate Drug-Target Interaction (DTI) prediction is critical for drug discovery. While deep learning advances this field, the fundamental lack of verified negative interactions inevitably causes biased risk estimation. Although formulating DTI prediction as a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning problem is theoretically sound, directly applying PU learning to deep models suffers from early-stage optimization instability and decision boundary ambiguity.
papers.summary: ProDTI addresses the lack of verified negative drug-target interactions by formulating DTI prediction as a positive-unlabeled learning problem, but adds prior guidance to overcome the early-stage optimization instability and decision boundary ambiguity that plague naive PU learning with deep models. The method aims to provide more robust and less biased DTI predictions for drug discovery.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: From Molecular Profiling to Personalized Clinical Management-A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease imposing a substantial health and economic burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to address CRS complexity in both clinical and research settings. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase for peer-reviewed articles utilizing machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, with a focus on molecular-level or immunologic mechanisms in CRS. Thirty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Our results de
papers.summary: This systematic review examines 31 studies applying machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing to chronic rhinosinusitis, with emphasis on molecular and immunologic mechanisms. It maps how AI is being used across molecular profiling and clinical management of this heterogeneous inflammatory disease, though the abstract is truncated before presenting detailed findings.

papers.title: Identification of YES1 Inhibitors From Approved Drugs Using a Multimodal Deep Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: While anti-human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) drugs, including trastuzumab improve the prognosis of patients with HER2-positive cancers, acquired resistance by cancer cells remains a significant clinical challenge. We had previously reported that YES1 is overexpressed in trastuzumab-resistant breast and lung cancer cells, and that its inhibition restores trastuzumab sensitivity. However, no approved drug specifically targets YES1. In this study, as a drug repositioning approach aimed at rapid clinical application, we constructed a machine learning model capable of learning the int
papers.summary: The authors built a multimodal deep learning framework to identify existing approved drugs that inhibit YES1, a kinase implicated in resistance to HER2-targeted therapies like trastuzumab. By screening approved drugs computationally, they aim to find candidates that could be rapidly repurposed to restore trastuzumab sensitivity in resistant breast and lung cancers. The work is a drug-repositioning effort combining machine learning with a specific clinical resistance problem.

papers.title: Novel Flavonoid Senotherapeutics Identified by Phenotypic Drug Discovery Reduce Senescence and Improve Multiple Markers of Healthspan.
papers.abstract: Senescent cells are a key driver of aging and contribute to many age-related diseases. Senolytics, agents that selectively eliminate senescent cells, offer a promising therapeutic strategy to treat age-related diseases but face significant barriers to clinical translation. Fisetin, a natural flavonoid senolytic, has progressed to clinical trials but is limited by suboptimal efficacy and poor bioavailability. To address these challenges, we developed two novel fisetin-derived flavonoid senolytics, SR29384 and SR31133, using an integrative phenotypic drug discovery approach. These compounds exhi
papers.summary: Researchers used a phenotypic drug discovery approach to create two new fisetin-derived flavonoid compounds, SR29384 and SR31133, that selectively target senescent cells. These compounds show improved senolytic activity and reduce senescence while improving multiple healthspan markers, potentially overcoming the poor efficacy and bioavailability of fisetin.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is a promising anticancer target, and the work demonstrates a hybrid computational pipeline for prioritizing natural-product candidates. The findings highlight marine compounds as a source of potential PIM-1 inhibitors for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Targeting a Leukemia-Relevant Protein-Protein Interface: N-Aryl Anthranilic Acids as Disruptors of the c-Myb-CBP/p300 KIX Interaction.
papers.abstract: The interaction between c-Myb and the CBP/p300 KIX domain is a key transcriptional event in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and represents an attractive target for small-molecule intervention. In this study, we applied an integrated computational-experimental strategy to identify new N-aryl anthranilic acid disruptors of the c-Myb-KIX protein-protein interaction. A scaffold-focused library of 3656 N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives was filtered, docked to the c-Myb-binding groove of KIX (PDB 2AGH), and the top hits were further evaluated by MD simulations, MM/PBSA, FEL, and ADMET analyses. This
papers.summary: The authors used a computational pipeline—library filtering, docking to the c-Myb-binding groove of the KIX domain, MD simulations, MM/PBSA, free energy landscape analysis, and ADMET prediction—to identify N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives that may disrupt the leukemia-relevant c-Myb–CBP/p300 KIX protein–protein interaction. This is an in silico hit-identification study; the abstract does not report experimental validation of the predicted disruptors.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified trans-thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. In benzylthiouracil (BTU)-treated Wistar rats, EO administration reduced the liver and kidney indices from 4.36% to 2.70% and from 0.65% to 0.52%, respectively; red blood cell count increased from 4.90 to 7.17 × 1012/L and hemoglobin from 9.40 to 15.40 g/dL. Aspartate aminot
papers.summary: This study characterizes the essential oil of Cotula cinerea, finding trans-thujone as its dominant component, and shows that the oil reduces liver and kidney swelling and improves blood parameters in rats with induced hypothyroidism. Histological and computational docking analyses support an anti-inflammatory effect, suggesting the oil's compounds may interact with inflammation-related targets.

papers.title: Synthesis and Cytotoxic Activity of 1,3-Selenazole-2-Amine Derivatives With Computational ADMET Profiling.
papers.abstract: A set of newly developed 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives (1-4) was prepared via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization of appropriately substituted α-bromoacetophenones with selenourea under reflux conditions. The synthesized compounds were tested for cytotoxic activity in HT-29 (colon cancer), MCF-7 (breast cancer), and L929 (mouse fibroblast) cell lines using the MTT assay. The compounds induced weak to moderate cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells. Among them, compound 4 showed cytotoxic activity with IC50 value of 171.10 µM, while no appreciable activity was observed against HT-29 cells (IC50 > 30
papers.summary: The authors synthesized four new 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives via a modified Hantzsch cyclization and tested them for cytotoxicity against colon (HT-29), breast (MCF-7), and normal fibroblast (L929) cell lines. The compounds showed only weak to moderate activity, with the best compound (4) having an IC50 of 171 µM against MCF-7 and no appreciable activity against HT-29. Computational ADMET profiling was also performed, but the overall biological activity is modest.

papers.title: Exploring the Neuropharmacological Potential of Ligustrum sinense Relevant to Parkinson's Disease: In Vivo and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are valuable sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders. This study investigated the antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities of Ligustrum sinense (L. sinense) leaf extract through in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. Antioxidant activity assessed by the DPPH assay demonstrated moderate free radical scavenging capacity (IC50 = 73.56 ± 2.18 µg/mL) compared with l-ascorbic acid (IC50 = 7.29 ± 2.86 µg/mL). Behavioral evaluations using the open field, hole cross, elevated plus maze,
papers.summary: This study evaluates leaf extracts of the medicinal plant Ligustrum sinense for antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities using in vitro, in vivo, and in silico methods, with a focus on relevance to Parkinson's disease. The extract showed moderate antioxidant capacity (DPPH IC50 ~73.6 µg/mL, weaker than ascorbic acid) and behavioral effects in rodent tests, with computational docking supporting possible MAO interactions. The work is preliminary and exploratory, lacking detailed compound characterization or mechanistic validation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences: Research output, trends, and thematic priorities - A descriptive analysis of web of science-indexed publications (2010-2025).
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences (PPS), yet the evolution, research priorities, and global landscape of AI-related research within this field have not been comprehensively characterized.
papers.journal: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
papers.summary: This study provides a descriptive bibliometric analysis of Web of Science-indexed publications from 2010 to 2025 on artificial intelligence in pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences. It characterizes the growth, research priorities, and global landscape of AI-related research in this field, which had not been comprehensively mapped before. The work offers a high-level overview of trends and thematic priorities rather than new methods or biological findings.

papers.title: Selective PTP1B inhibition by A-1331852: Uncompetitive kinetics and computational evidence for C-terminal engagement.
papers.abstract: Selective inhibition of protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B), a well-established target in metabolic and oncological signaling pathways, is limited by its 74% active-site identity with the closely related phosphatase TCPTP. Repurposing the clinical-stage Bcl-xL BH3 mimetic A-1331852, we identify it as a potent PTP1B inhibitor demonstrating a selectivity margin of at least 50-fold over TCPTP (IC₅₀ = 4.0 μM vs >200 μM). Kinetic analysis reveals uncompetitive inhibition consistent with recognition of a substrate-induced binding site. Docking and 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations (MD) of fu
papers.summary: The clinical-stage Bcl-xL inhibitor A-1331852 was found to potently inhibit PTP1B with at least 50-fold selectivity over the closely related phosphatase TCPTP. Kinetic analysis indicates uncompetitive inhibition, suggesting binding to a substrate-induced site, and docking plus 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations support engagement of a C-terminal region rather than the conserved active site. This offers a potential repurposing route and a strategy to overcome the selectivity challenge caused by high active-site homology.

papers.title: Enzymatic N-deacylation is the predicted membrane-disruption switch for sphingomyelin: a falsifiable in-silico framework for sphingolipid vulnerability in ALS.
papers.abstract: Sphingolipid dysregulation is an emerging feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but no systematic method separates species that may worsen axon-myelin membrane integrity from matter that may counteract it. We present an in-silico framework classifying sphingolipids and designed derivatives as candidate membrane-disruptive or candidate protective species, scored against real biological referents using externally published tools rather than a bespoke composite. Its central finding concerns a single, chemically defined difference in lipid state. In coarse-grained (MARTINI 3) molecular d
papers.summary: The authors present an in-silico framework that classifies sphingolipids and designed derivatives as either membrane-disruptive or protective, using published tools rather than a custom composite score. The central claim is that enzymatic N-deacylation of sphingomyelin acts as a predicted membrane-disruption switch, framed as a falsifiable hypothesis relevant to sphingolipid vulnerability in ALS. The abstract is truncated, so the full scope of the coarse-grained MARTINI 3 simulations is not visible.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and genome mining strategies for activating cryptic polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces: an overview.
papers.abstract: Beneficial microbes from soil or marine habitats are promising sources for discovery of new bioactive compounds for medicine and agriculture, largely through biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) that encode the production of complex natural products for drug and antibiotic discovery. However, most BGCs are transcriptionally silent under standard testing conditions and may require a complex, integrated approach for activation. In this review, we revisit previous approaches to activating BGCs, focusing on polyketides. We additionally discuss how integrating genome mining strategies with multi-omics
papers.summary: This review surveys strategies for activating silent polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces, which are a major source of natural-product drugs but often remain transcriptionally inactive under standard lab conditions. It emphasizes combining genome mining with multi-omics approaches to identify and trigger these cryptic clusters, expanding the pool of discoverable bioactive compounds for medicine and agriculture.

papers.title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrated multi-model AI pipelines can accelerate the discovery and design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) as alternatives to conventional antibiotics in the face of rising antimicrobial resistance. It highlights how AI can help overcome key bottlenecks such as peptide instability, potency, and cytotoxicity that hinder clinical translation. The paper frames AI-driven in silico discovery as a transformative strategy for the post-antibiotic era.

papers.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A co
papers.summary: MolecureAI is an autonomous AI agent platform for closed-loop drug discovery that selects design strategies, maintains structural memory across campaigns, applies in-loop ADMET safety gating, and integrates literature-scale evidence into molecular generation. The system enforces chemical correctness through structural invariants rather than relying solely on model capability, aiming to accelerate identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas.

papers.title: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
papers.abstract: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. While surgical interventions achieve acute stone clearance, they do not resolve underlying metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, or chronic inflammatory cascades. Natural products from global ethnomedicinal systems (including Traditional Chinese Medicine, Indian Ayurveda, Persian Unani medicine, European phytotherapy, and African ethnopharmacology) demonstrate potent multi-target anti-urolithic properties. However, de
papers.summary: This review surveys how network pharmacology approaches are being used to understand the multi-target mechanisms by which natural products from various ethnomedicinal traditions inhibit kidney stone formation. It argues that these compounds act on multiple pathways simultaneously—addressing metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, and inflammation—which single-target surgical or pharmacological approaches do not resolve. The paper synthesizes evidence on anti-urolithic natural products and the network-based methods used to dissect their mechanisms.

papers.title: Knowledge graph and machine learning-guided virtual screening prioritizes putative blockers of the PSMD11/Rpn6-EBOV glycoprotein interface.
papers.abstract: Host-directed antiviral discovery requires a traceable route from host-factor identification to testable molecular hypotheses. This study developed such a workflow around a host factor associated with Ebola virus glycoprotein (EBOV GP).
papers.summary: This study presents a workflow that combines knowledge graph analysis and machine learning to prioritize putative small-molecule blockers of the interaction between the host protein PSMD11/Rpn6 and the Ebola virus glycoprotein. The approach provides a traceable path from host-factor identification to virtual screening and testable molecular hypotheses for host-directed antiviral discovery.

papers.title: Commentary: Identification of diagnostic genes for myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury associated with metabolic syndrome through the integration of bioinformatics analysis, molecular docking and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a study that used bioinformatics integration, molecular docking, and experimental validation to identify diagnostic genes for myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in the context of metabolic syndrome. It likely highlights the study's approach and findings while offering critical perspective on the methodology and clinical implications. As a commentary, it does not present new primary data but contextualizes the original research.

papers.title: Single‑Cell in silico Perturbation Uncovers a Ferroptosis Regulatory Network for Cigarette Smoke‑Induced Skin Aging and Identifies Dapivirine as a Candidate Agent.
papers.abstract: Cigarette smoke exposure induces cutaneous ferroptosis and accelerates skin aging, yet the core regulatory genes and targeted interventions remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key ferroptosis-driving genes underlying smoke-induced skin senescence, clarify their mechanisms, and screen candidate small molecules that reverse smoke-related skin damage.
papers.summary: The study uses single-cell in silico perturbation analysis to identify a ferroptosis-related regulatory network driving cigarette smoke-induced skin aging, then screens for small molecules that reverse this signature, nominating dapivirine as a candidate agent. It links smoke exposure to cutaneous ferroptosis and proposes a computational drug-repurposing path for skin senescence.

papers.title: Integrated counter current separation and omics approaches for discovery of bioactive compounds from medicinal plants.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants provide an important source of structurally varied bioactive metabolites with medicinal potential; however, their effective extraction, characterization, and standardization present considerable analytical challenges. Counter-current separation (CCS) methods, such as centrifugal partition chromatography (CPC) and high-speed counter-current chromatography (HSCCC), represent advanced liquid-liquid chromatographic approaches that minimize irreversible adsorption of samples. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Sci
papers.summary: This review examines how counter-current separation methods (CPC and HSCCC) can be integrated with omics approaches to discover and characterize bioactive compounds from medicinal plants. The authors argue that these liquid-liquid chromatographic techniques reduce irreversible sample adsorption and, when combined with metabolomics and other omics workflows, offer a more effective pipeline for isolating, identifying, and standardizing plant-derived bioactive metabolites.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling uncovers an aging-associated ETS1-MYO1B vascular niche responsive to ipragliflozin.
papers.abstract: Tissue aging involves complex changes in vascular, immune, and stromal compartments that collectively reshape the local tissue ecosystem and may contribute to age-related diseases, including cancer, fibrotic diseases, and cardiovascular disease. However, it remains unclear whether reproducible, cell-specific vascular niche states emerge during aging and whether these states can be therapeutically targeted.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using multimodal profiling, the authors identify a reproducible aging-associated vascular niche state marked by ETS1-MYO1B expression that emerges across tissues during aging. They show this niche can be therapeutically modulated by ipragliflozin, suggesting a druggable target for age-related vascular dysfunction. The work links aging, vascular remodeling, and a potential pharmacological intervention.

papers.title: Lightweight 2D-Convolutional Neural Network for Drug-Kinase Binding Affinity Prediction with Minimal Encoded Representations.
papers.abstract: Drug-kinase binding affinity (DKBA) prediction plays a crucial role in prioritizing compounds and reducing the time and financial resources required for drug discovery. However, many existing deep learning models rely on complex molecular representations, such as molecular graphs or pretrained embeddings, which may increase computational complexity and limit scalability.
papers.journal: Iranian journal of pharmaceutical research : IJPR
papers.summary: The paper introduces a lightweight 2D-convolutional neural network that predicts drug-kinase binding affinity using minimal encoded molecular representations, avoiding complex graphs or pretrained embeddings. This reduces computational cost and improves scalability while maintaining useful predictive performance for compound prioritization in drug discovery.

papers.title: Advances in deep learning for antimicrobial research.
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of antimicrobial resistance and the lag in the development of new antimicrobial drugs have become major challenges for global public health. Conventional methods for discovering antimicrobial drugs are characterized by long development cycles and high costs, which are further exacerbated by the rapid evolution of bacterial resistance. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop efficient computational methods to accelerate the identification of drug resistance mechanisms and the research and development process of new antimicrobial drugs. In recent years, the new generation
papers.summary: This review surveys recent deep learning approaches applied to antimicrobial research, covering both the identification of resistance mechanisms and the acceleration of new antimicrobial drug discovery. It argues that conventional experimental pipelines are too slow and costly to keep pace with resistance evolution, and that computational methods offer a promising route to speed up target identification and candidate screening.

papers.title: AI-guided ethnopharmacology for cardiovascular drug discovery: from biomedical data to experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Botanical drugs represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites, yet their translation into modern cardiovascular therapeutics remains limited by chemical complexity, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and challenges in experimental validation. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of biomedical data resources and advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have created new opportunities to systematically investigate botanical drugs beyond empirical a
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can be combined with ethnopharmacology to accelerate the discovery of cardiovascular drugs from botanical sources. It argues that AI-driven analysis of large biomedical datasets can help overcome the chemical complexity and mechanistic gaps that have limited the translation of plant-derived compounds into modern cardiovascular therapeutics, and it outlines a path from data mining to experimental validation.

papers.title: Potential Molecular Links Between Benzophenone-3 and Breast Cancer: Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Molecular Modeling, and Gene Expression Validation.
papers.abstract: Benzophenone-3 (BP-3) is a widely used ultraviolet filter with potential carcinogenic concern, but its molecular link with breast cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate targets and potential molecular links between BP-3 and breast cancer using toxicological prediction, machine learning, molecular modeling, and gene expression analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking, and gene expression data to identify candidate molecular targets linking the UV filter benzophenone-3 (BP-3) to breast cancer. The authors propose potential target genes and pathways that could mediate BP-3-associated breast cancer risk, though the findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Placental alkaline phosphatase promotes lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy and represents a potential target for statin repurposing.
papers.abstract: Lumbar spinal stenosis is a prevalent degenerative disorder driven primarily by ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Emerging evidence links ectopic lipid accumulation to fibrotic remodeling and suggests a potential contribution of immune dysregulation. However, the molecular targets connecting lipid accumulation with ligamentum flavum fibrosis remain incompletely defined. We sought to evaluate the underlying mechanisms of lipid-lowering drug targets in lipid-associated ligamentum flavum fibrosis.
papers.summary: This study identifies placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) as a molecular link between ectopic lipid accumulation and fibrotic remodeling in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, a key driver of lumbar spinal stenosis. The authors propose that statins, via lipid-lowering effects, may be repurposed to target PLAP and reduce fibrosis, offering a potential pharmacological strategy for this degenerative disorder.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore ana
papers.summary: This study combines a 3D convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder with LSTM-based molecular generation to design novel rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors for restless legs syndrome. Fourteen unique candidates were generated and filtered through pocket prediction, docking, interaction profiling, and pharmacophore analysis. The work demonstrates a generative deep-learning pipeline for structure-guided drug design, though experimental validation of the candidates is not reported.

papers.title: Identification of flavonoids from natural products against hyperlipidaemia through computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Over the centuries, hyperlipidaemia has been recognised as a major risk factor contributing to cardiovascular disease (CVD). Current research increasingly explores natural compounds such as flavonoids for their potential lipid-lowering effects. This study evaluated pharmacological potential of flavonoids to identify strong inhibitors for target receptor, Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type (PCSK9). A total of 29 compounds, including one FDA-approved drugs were screened for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using PC
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 29 flavonoids (plus one FDA-approved drug) for drug-likeness, ADMET properties, and binding to PCSK9, a key cholesterol-regulating target. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to identify flavonoids with strong predicted binding affinity to PCSK9. The work proposes candidate natural compounds for lipid-lowering therapy, though experimental validation is absent.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study computationally screens phytochemicals from the mangrove plant Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of proteins implicated in non-small cell lung cancer. Using molecular docking, dynamics simulations, and other in silico analyses, the authors identify candidate compounds with favorable binding and predicted drug-like properties. The work is purely computational and provides hypotheses for experimental validation rather than demonstrated anticancer activity.

papers.title: Preclinical identification of an oxadiazole-pyrazole lead targeting prostate cancer through integrated mechanistic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men, while resistance to androgen deprivation therapy emphasizes the need for new therapeutic strategies. Molecular hybridization of pharmacologically relevant heterocycles offers a rational approach for developing novel anticancer agents.
papers.summary: This study reports the preclinical identification of a novel oxadiazole-pyrazole hybrid compound as a lead for prostate cancer therapy, motivated by the need for alternatives to androgen deprivation therapy. The authors use integrated mechanistic evaluation to characterize the compound's anticancer activity, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific targets or in vivo results.
